title: 380 Million Monarch Butterflies Once Filled One Mexican Forest

scenes.text: 380 million butterflies once filled one forest.
In the winter of 1996 to 1997, monarchs covered over 18 hectares in Mexico.
That's about 21 million butterflies on every hectare.
They roost in dense clusters, mostly in oyamel fir trees.
In 2013 to 2014, the colonies shrank to about 14 million.
From 380 million to 14 million, in less than 20 winters.

description:
In the winter of 1996 to 1997, an estimated 380 million monarch butterflies filled over 18 hectares of forest in central Mexico.
By 2013 to 2014 the count had fallen to about 14 million.
Have you ever seen a monarch?
first_comment: Have you ever seen a monarch up close?
